rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some identify taghut as Satan; since Satan prompts idol worship, worshipping idols counts as serving Satan.
rows.anchor: فقيل إنه الشيطان فإن قيل إنهم ما عبدوا الشيطان وإنما عبدوا الصنم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Others call idols taghuts metaphorically: worshipers transgress, but idols are named for the transgression their sight and proximity cause.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالطاغوت الصنم وسميت طواغيت على سبيل المجاز لأنه لا فعل لها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view defines taghut as anything worshipped or obeyed apart from God.
rows.anchor: وقيل كل ما يعبد ويطاع من دون الله فهو طاغوت

rows.speaker: في التواريخ
rows.claim: Historical accounts say idol worship began with anthropomorphists imagining God as a great light and angels as lights of differing sizes, then worshipping images made to match them.
rows.anchor: ويقال في التواريخ إن الأصل في عبادة الأصنام ، أن القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi sums up avoiding taghut as turning from servitude to everything besides God, and inaba as returning wholly to worship of God.
rows.anchor: أي أعرضوا عن عبودية كل ما سوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Citing a Torah instruction to answer God with the whole heart, Razi says exclusive devotion does not mean denying created causes; God alone is necessary, while all else is contingent and depends on His bringing it into being.
rows.anchor: يا موسى أجب إلهك بكل قلبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God arranges some events through intermediaries and others without them; all things are from God, and He alone is the ultimate manager and effective agent.
rows.anchor: جعل تكوينه للأشياء على قسمين منها ما يكون بغير واسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi recounts advising a young man to protect his reputation and wealth; the youth invoked reliance on decree, but Razi said he had misunderstood a true principle.
rows.anchor: وقد اتفق أني كنت أنصح بعض الصبيان في حفظ العرض والمال فعارضني وقالا يجوز الاعتماد على الجد والجهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For events in this lower world, God has appointed known causes; the higher world has events without intermediaries.
rows.anchor: فهو حوادث هذا العالم الأسفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking lower-world outcomes without the means God assigned opposes His wisdom and ordering; reliance on God is compatible with using those means.
rows.anchor: من طلب حوادث هذا العالم الأسفل لا من الأسباب التي عينها الله تعالى كان هذا الشخص منازعا لله في حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised glad tidings come near death, in the grave, at the gathering, at the division of the saved and damned, and upon believers' entry into Paradise.
rows.anchor: إنها تحصل عند القرب من الموت وعند الوضع في القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tidings remove fear of future judgment and grief over lost worldly good, then announce Paradise and its delights and lasting fulfillment.
rows.anchor: والخوف إنما يكون من المستقبل والحزن إنما يكون بسبب الأحوال الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels may give the glad tidings at death and on entering Paradise; God may also give them when the believers meet Him.
rows.anchor: فنقول يحتمل أن يكون هم الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted phrase implies exclusivity: this glad tidings belongs to those who avoid worship of anything besides God and turn wholly to Him.
rows.anchor: أي لهم لا لغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-bushra suggests the entire kind of glad tidings belongs to them, leaving no share for others.
rows.anchor: أن الألف واللام في لفظ البشرى مفيد للماهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since glad tidings are the first announcement of good, rewards already known in worldly life would merely repeat old news; the tidings therefore promise further bliss, including what no soul knows.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن هذه البشارة لا تتحقق إلا إذا حصل الإخبار بحصول أنواع أخر من السعادات فوق ما عرفوها وسمعوها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God Himself announces the reward after such a demanding condition, its greatness exceeds what minds can fully describe.
rows.anchor: هو الله تعالى وهو أعظم العظماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi identifies the servants to be given glad tidings as the ones who shunned taghut and returned to God; naming them explicitly ties wholehearted devotion to listening and following the best.
rows.anchor: الذين اجتنبوا وأنابوا لا غيرهم وهذا يدل على أن رأس السعادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit noun phrase replaces an expected pronoun to signal that the previous God-turned servants are the listeners who follow the best.
rows.anchor: على هذا الحرف ، ومنهم من قال

rows.speaker: منهم
rows.claim: Another view broadens the promise: anyone who chooses the best in every matter joins the saved, avoiding a restriction that would exclude most people from mercy.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال إنه تعالى لما بين أن الذين اجتنبوا وأنابوا لهم البشرى وكان ذلك درجة عالية لا يصل إليها إلا الأولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse makes guidance depend on hearing many claims and choosing the soundest; because hearing is shared by all, reason rather than hearing distinguishes the best and merits praise.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنه تعالى بين أن الهداية والفلاح مرتبطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religions can be assessed by detailed proofs and rebuttals, or first by comparing them and accepting what sound reason judges more excellent before detailed inquiry.
rows.anchor: قبل البحث عن الدلائل وتقريرها والشبهات وتزييفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Initial rational comparison favors affirming a living, knowing, powerful, wise, merciful God; divine sovereignty; God's unity and freedom from composition; independence from space and time; and the possibility of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: صمد منزه عن التركيب والأعضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among prayers, Razi prefers the form with intention at the opening takbir, al-Fatiha, tranquility in the five postures, tashahhud, and ending with salutation over one lacking these features.
rows.anchor: وتكون النية فيها مقارنة للتكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although retaliation, blood money, and pardon are legislated, God encourages pardon as nearer to piety.
rows.anchor: ولكنه ندب إلى العفو فقال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says this refers to a person who hears good and bad in a gathering, then relates the best report and leaves the rest.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس / أن المراد منه الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance requires an agent and a recipient: God is the agent, while the human soul is the receptive locus, identified as the people of understanding.
rows.anchor: أمر حادث ، ولا بد له من فاعل وقابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul and its rational light can receive either true or false belief equally, so the recipient cannot itself cause one to prevail; as a body equally receptive to motion and rest cannot select either, God must cause guidance.
rows.anchor: قابل للاعتقاد الحق والاعتقاد الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Appealing to a will does not solve the problem: the soul is also equally receptive to the contrary will, so it cannot originate the preference that produces guidance.
rows.anchor: فكذلك ذات العقل قابلة لإرادة مضادة لتلك الإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi raises a grammatical puzzle: Arabic does not normally place an interrogative over both a nominal subject and its predicate, yet here the interrogative and fāʾ appear with both conditional and consequent.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح في الكلام العربي أن يدخل حرف الاستفهام على الاسم وعلى الخبر معا

words: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ من في النار
rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i parses the wording as three questions: whether the sentence of punishment has taken effect, whether the Prophet can protect that person, and whether he can rescue those in the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي : الآية جملتنا والتقدير

words: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ من في النار
rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's Kashshaf treats it as one conditional question: an initial fāʾ coordinates with an omitted clause inferred from the address, while the repeated hamza intensifies denial and those in the Fire replaces a pronoun.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : أصل الكلام

words: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ من في النار
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi also explains the repeated interrogative as intensifying the complete denial: it is repeated over both condition and consequence because the rejection is emphatic.
rows.anchor: ذكر هذا الحرف في الشرط وأعاده في الجزاء

rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: The Ash'ari theologians argue that one for whom punishment is decreed cannot perform faith and obedience; otherwise God's true statement would become false and His knowledge ignorance.
rows.anchor: احتج الأصحاب بهذه الآية في مسألة الهدى والضلال

words: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ من في النار
rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: A second Ash'ari argument says the verse's emphatic denial of rescuing the condemned makes sense only if the decree of punishment prevents their faith and obedience.
rows.anchor: في الاستدلال بالآية أنه تعالى حكم بأن

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi argues that the Prophet cannot intercede for major sinners, since they are condemned and intercession would amount to rescuing them from the Fire.
rows.anchor: احتج القاضي بهذه الآية على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يشفع لأهل الكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the premise that major sinners are certainly condemned: God says He may forgive sins below associating partners and that He forgives all sins.
rows.anchor: لا نسلم أن أهل الكبائر قد حق عليهم العذاب

words: لهم غرف من فوقها غرف مبنية
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised upper chambers contrast with the disbelievers' layers of fire above and below them.
rows.anchor: وهذا كالمقابل لما ذكر في وصف الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though an upper storey is usually weaker than the one beneath, Paradise's chambers combine height with the strength of the lower storeys.
rows.anchor: لأن المنزل إذا بنى على منزل آخر تحته كان الفوقاني أضعف بناء من التحتاني

rows.speaker: حكماء الإسلام
rows.claim: Islamic philosophers liken the tiered chambers to acquired sciences built upon one another, culminating in knowledge of God's essence and attributes as strong as first principles.
rows.anchor: وقال حكماء الإسلام هذه الغرف المبنية بعضها فوق البعض

words: وعد الله لا يخلف الله الميعاد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reads the repeated assurance that God fulfills His promise as evidence that promise outweighs threat, against the Mu'tazilite position.
rows.anchor: في كثير من آيات الوعد صرح بأن هذا وعد الله

words: وعد الله لا يخلف الله الميعاد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counterexample that God does not change His word is general, applying to both promise and threat, so it does not specifically reinforce the threat.
rows.anchor: قلنا قوله ما يبدل القول لدي ليس تصريحا بجانب الوعيد بل هو كلام عام يتناول القسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water is rain; an alternative view says everything on earth comes from the sky. God sends the water to places, then distributes it through springs, channels, and underground courses like bodily veins.
rows.anchor: وهو المطر وقيل كل ما كان في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop's differing colors may mean different hues such as green, red, yellow, and white, or different kinds such as wheat, barley, and sesame.
rows.anchor: يخرج به زرعا مختلفا ألوانه من خضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After fully drying, the crop can detach from its roots before its parts break apart; it is as if the parts have stirred in readiness to disperse.
rows.anchor: إذا تم جفافه جاز له أن ينفصل عن منابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hutam is the dry plant matter that crumbles and breaks apart.
rows.anchor: والحطام ما يجف ويتفتت ويكسر من النبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Watching plants age reminds people that animals and humans, however long-lived, will grow old, become yellow and broken, and die; this reflection makes worldly pleasures less alluring.
rows.anchor: علم أن أحوال الحيوان والإنسان كذلك وأنه وإن طال عمره فلا بد له من الانتهاء إلى أن يصير مصفر اللون منحطم الأعضاء والأجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding descriptions of the afterlife promote desire for it, while this world's description promotes aversion; direct encouragement toward the afterlife comes first because it is the primary aim.
rows.anchor: في الآيات المتقدمة ذكر ما يقوى الرغبة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi derives yanabi from yanbu, on the pattern yaf'ul, from the root n-b-ʿ; al-Kisa'i and al-Farra report three forms for the verb meaning water bubbled forth.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : والينابيع جمع ينبوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanabi is accusative with the preposition omitted; the underlying phrase is to direct the water into springs.
rows.anchor: نصب بحذف الخافض لأن التقدير فسلكه في ينابيع

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: In the lexical discussion, al-Wahidi glosses yahiij as becoming green.
rows.anchor: ثم يهيج أي يخضر

none: quoted neighboring verses only; no commentary
